hypothesis: The parent's density-weight relaxations all act on the *global* density weight, but the real TNS cost comes from a few congested bins forcing detours. Instead of further loosening the global weight, I will make the early-iteration damping smoother (quadratic ramp over a longer window) so the density weight grows gradually and the placer spends more iterations in a low-congestion, wirelength-friendly regime before density pressure ramps up — this should reduce congestion-driven detours (overflow) and let the timing repair see shorter nets, lowering TNS broadly without starving density (the ramp still reaches full strength by iteration 100).
expected_effect: WNS same or slightly better; TNS improved (more moderate violations removed); overflow same or lower; runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: all three cases improved, with robust score +0.135 and no invalid runs. Gains are broad—dTNS +12.9% to +31.4%, dWNS +9.1% to +23.4%—consistent with the mechanism: a smoother quadratic ramp keeps the placer in a wirelength-friendly, low-overflow regime longer, so timing repair sees shorter nets. Overflow (~84–104) stayed controlled, so density wasn't starved. Next step: sweep the ramp window length (e.g., 80/100/120 iterations) and curvature to find whether a longer or gentler ramp yields further TNS gains without overflow regressing.
